package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally crafted to exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the CDNJS automated update infrastructure. By including files and symlinks with malicious paths in the npm tarball, the attacker could achieve arbitrary file write and remote code execution on Cloudflare's CDNJS servers. This attack could result in full compromise of the CDNJS infrastructure, enabling supply-chain attacks on millions of websites.

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate (CI/CD bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) containing files with path traversal sequences in their archive paths (e.g., '../../../tmp/ryotak.sh')

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (bash script, delivered via crafted archive path)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Places a shell script outside the intended extraction directory using path traversal in the archive entry, enabling arbitrary code execution on the server if the script is executed by automation or CI/CD processes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of multiple '../' (dot-dot-slash) sequences in archive file paths is a classic indicator of a path traversal attack, commonly known as 'ZIP Slip'. This technique is used to escape the intended extraction directory and write files to arbitrary locations on the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should only contain files within their own directory structure. This package attempts to write files to arbitrary locations on the server filesystem, violating package isolation and integrity expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Path traversal in archive files is almost never legitimate in package distribution. Legitimate packages should not contain files with '../' in their paths.
key_indicators: Archive entries with multiple '../' sequences in file paths
Files written to /tmp or other system directories outside the package scope
Presence of executable scripts placed outside the package extraction directory

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate (CI/CD bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) containing a symlink with a target outside the package directory (e.g., symlink to /etc/passwd or configuration files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: symlink in git repo pointing to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd or config files)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Creates a symbolic link in the package archive that, when extracted by the bot, points to sensitive files on the server (such as /etc/passwd). This allows the attacker to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem if the bot or automation process follows the symlink.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Symlinks in package archives that point outside the package directory are a known method for arbitrary file read attacks. This can expose sensitive files to the attacker if the automation process reads or processes the symlink.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not contain symlinks to sensitive system files or files outside their own directory. Package archives are expected to be self-contained and not reference external system paths.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Symlinks are sometimes used for internal package structure, but never to system files or locations outside the package directory.
key_indicators: Symlinks in package archives pointing to /etc, /tmp, or other sensitive locations
Symlinks present in the package root or in unexpected locations
Symlinks with absolute or traversal-based targets outside the package scope

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate (CI/CD bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) containing files with path traversal sequences targeting automation or CI/CD scripts (e.g., '../../../path/to/regularly_executed_script')

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (bash script, delivered via crafted archive path)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Overwrites a script that is regularly executed by the CDNJS update bot or automation system, enabling persistent arbitrary command execution by replacing trusted automation code with attacker-controlled code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overwriting system or automation scripts via path traversal is a direct method to gain persistent code execution. This allows the attacker to execute arbitrary commands every time the automation runs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Package updates should never overwrite automation or system scripts outside their own directory. Such behavior breaks the trust boundary between package content and system integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for overwriting automation or system scripts via package updates in package management.
key_indicators: Archive entries targeting automation or system scripts outside the package directory
Unexpected changes to bot or CI/CD scripts after package update
Executable files in system or automation directories modified by package extraction

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a new npm package (hey-sven) with maliciously crafted archive paths, including path traversal entries and symlinks targeting sensitive files and system locations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious files and symlinks are included in the package archive, setting up the payload for exploitation.

attack_chain.action: CDNJS autoupdate bot downloads and extracts the new package version, processing the malicious archive and extracting files and symlinks to unintended locations on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Path traversal and symlink payloads are written to arbitrary locations on the server, including system directories and automation script paths.

attack_chain.action: Malicious scripts are executed by the bot or automation system, or sensitive files are accessed via symlink, enabling the attacker to execute arbitrary code or exfiltrate secrets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution and/or access to sensitive secrets (API keys, tokens) present on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen secrets (such as GITHUB_REPO_API_KEY, WORKERS_KV_API_TOKEN) to tamper with CDNJS libraries, cache, or website content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of CDNJS infrastructure and potential supply-chain attack on all users of the CDN.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction with file paths containing multiple '../' sequences (path traversal)
Symlinks in package archives pointing outside the package directory (e.g., to /etc/passwd or /tmp)
Unexpected file writes or overwrites in /tmp, /etc, or automation script directories during package extraction
Execution of scripts extracted from package archives that reside outside the intended package scope
file_indicators: npm package tarballs (.tgz) containing archive entries with '../' in file paths
Symlinks in package archives with targets outside the package directory (absolute or traversal-based)
Overwritten automation or CI/CD scripts (e.g., update bots, deployment scripts) after package update
network_indicators: Unusual access to internal API endpoints using newly extracted secrets (e.g., GITHUB_REPO_API_KEY, WORKERS_KV_API_TOKEN)
Unexpected outbound connections or data exfiltration attempts from automation bots following a package update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor and scan package archives for file paths containing path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../../'). Block or alert on symlinks in package archives that point outside the package directory. Audit automation and CI/CD scripts for unexpected changes or overwrites after package updates. Monitor for use of sensitive secrets (API keys, tokens) from unexpected locations or processes, especially after package updates. Implement sandboxing and filesystem restrictions (e.g., AppArmor, chroot) for automation bots to prevent file system escape and privilege escalation.
